title: Boolean Retrieval and Inverted Indexes
abstract: Explains Boolean retrieval using AND, OR and NOT operators. An inverted index maps each term to the documents containing it, enabling efficient set-based retrieval.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: The Vector Space Model for Document Retrieval
abstract: Represents documents and queries as weighted term vectors. Similarity between a query and document can be measured using cosine similarity in a high-dimensional term space.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Information Retrieval: An Introduction
abstract: Introduces the goals of information retrieval, document collections, indexing, query processing, ranking, and evaluation of search systems.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Tokenization and Text Normalization
abstract: Describes splitting text into tokens and normalizing case, punctuation, and word forms before indexing. Consistent preprocessing improves matching between queries and documents.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Stop Word Removal in Search
abstract: Discusses removing very common words such as the, is, and of to reduce index size and limit low-value matches. Stop word removal can sometimes remove meaningful terms.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Stemming and Lemmatization
abstract: Compares reducing words to stems with mapping inflected words to dictionary base forms. These normalization methods can improve recall when users search with different word forms.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Phrase Queries and Positional Indexes
abstract: Explains how positional indexes store token positions so a search engine can match exact phrases and terms occurring near one another.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Spelling Correction and Query Suggestions
abstract: Covers spelling correction, edit distance, and query suggestions that help users recover from typographical errors and express their information need.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Term Frequency and Document Frequency
abstract: Defines term frequency as the number of occurrences of a term in a document and document frequency as the number of documents containing that term.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: TF-IDF Weighting for Search Ranking
abstract: Explains term frequency inverse document frequency weighting. Terms frequent in a document but rare across the collection receive higher weights and can distinguish relevant documents.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Cosine Similarity in Text Retrieval
abstract: Describes cosine similarity as the normalized dot product between query and document vectors. It compares vector direction and is commonly used with TF-IDF representations.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: BM25 Probabilistic Ranking
abstract: Introduces BM25 as a probabilistic ranking function using term frequency saturation, inverse document frequency, and document length normalization.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Document Length Normalization
abstract: Explains why long documents may contain more term matches simply because they contain more words. Length normalization adjusts scores to avoid unfair advantages for long records.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Title and Field Weighting in Search
abstract: Studies assigning greater importance to terms in titles, headings, and other fields than in body text. Field weighting can improve ranking when titles summarize document topics.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Query Expansion with Synonyms
abstract: Explains adding related words and synonyms to a query to retrieve documents that use different vocabulary. Expansion may improve recall but can introduce irrelevant results.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Relevance Feedback in Information Retrieval
abstract: Describes using user judgments on initial search results to refine a query or update term weights, helping the system move toward more relevant documents.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Precision and Recall for Search Evaluation
abstract: Defines precision as the fraction of retrieved documents that are relevant and recall as the fraction of all relevant documents that are retrieved.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Precision at K for Ranked Retrieval
abstract: Explains Precision at K as the proportion of the top K ranked results that are relevant. It emphasizes the quality of the first results shown to a searcher.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Mean Average Precision
abstract: Introduces average precision across recall levels and mean average precision across multiple queries as measures for evaluating ranked retrieval systems.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: NDCG and Graded Relevance
abstract: Explains normalized discounted cumulative gain, which rewards highly relevant documents near the top of a ranking and supports graded relevance judgments.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Test Collections and Relevance Judgments
abstract: Describes building evaluation collections with documents, test queries, and relevance judgments. Consistent judgments make comparisons between retrieval methods meaningful.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: A/B Testing Search Ranking Changes
abstract: Discusses comparing alternative ranking systems using controlled experiments, user interaction measures, and offline relevance metrics.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Web Crawling and Search Indexing
abstract: Explains how crawlers discover web pages, fetch content, follow links, and provide pages for indexing by a search engine.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Link Analysis and PageRank
abstract: Describes using the web link graph to estimate page importance. PageRank distributes importance through incoming links and complements text-based relevance.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Search Engine Index Construction
abstract: Covers collecting documents, parsing content, building dictionaries and postings lists, and storing indexes to support efficient query execution.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Distributed Information Retrieval
abstract: Explains partitioning indexes and processing queries across multiple machines. Distributed retrieval improves scalability for very large document collections.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Learning to Rank for Search
abstract: Introduces machine learning methods that combine query-document features to rank results using training data and relevance labels.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Neural Information Retrieval
abstract: Surveys neural methods that encode queries and documents into dense representations. Semantic matching can retrieve relevant content even when exact words differ.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval
abstract: Explains dual-encoder retrieval where query and passage embeddings are compared, often using inner product or vector similarity to find semantically related passages.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Evaluation of Search Systems with User Studies
abstract: Covers user-centered evaluation including task success, satisfaction, click behavior, and time to find information, complementing offline metrics.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Natural Language Processing for Search
abstract: Explains how NLP techniques such as entity recognition, language modeling, and semantic analysis can improve query understanding and document retrieval.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Named Entity Recognition in Search
abstract: Describes identifying people, places, organizations, and other named entities in text. Entity-aware search can disambiguate queries and improve precision.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Semantic Search and Word Embeddings
abstract: Explains semantic search using word or sentence embeddings to capture meaning and relationships beyond exact keyword overlap.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Federated Search Across Multiple Sources
abstract: Describes searching multiple independent collections and merging their ranked results, including score normalization and source selection.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Privacy and Security in Search Logs
abstract: Discusses privacy risks in query logs, data minimization, access controls, retention limits, and protecting sensitive user search activity.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.

title: Multilingual Information Retrieval
abstract: Explains retrieving documents across languages using translation, multilingual representations, and language-aware tokenization and normalization.
source_note: Original educational summary; see linked Information Retrieval / NIST reference for background.
